we have identified 12 chromosomal segments, ranging in size from 0.7 to 10.5 cM, that are identical by descent in several patients and are located in regions that have previously been proposed to contain susceptibility loci for schizophrenia.

we have identified 11 chromosomal regions inherited identically in three or more patients, and that at least four are ancestral, and five others are possibly so, since the frequency of the haplotypes is significantly higher in patients compared to controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of ancestral chromosomal regions that may harbour schizophrenia susceptibility genes.
the identification of chromosomal segments that are inherited in the same form from an ancient common ancestor and that are more frequent in affected individuals than in unrelated controls.
identifying ancestral haplotype regions that are inherited identical by descent from an ancestral couple and that are associated with schizophrenia.

the 12 genomic regions are ancestral and that they contain susceptibility genes for this disorder.

we have identified several ancestral haplotypes that are associated with schizophrenia and that may harbour schizophrenia susceptibility locis.
the 12-generations schizophrenia pedigree provides an excellent resource for the study of complex disorders.

the haplotype analysis of large pedigrees may provide new insights into the genetic architecture of schizophrenia.
